title: A strict interval-attachment model for derived simplicial localization
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, the Dwyer--Kan model structure, its cofibrations, the homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$, and derived localization $L_VD$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], in fixed containing universes. Let $[1]$ be the discrete two-object walking arrow, and $\mathbb J$ the discrete two-object groupoid with exactly one arrow between each ordered pair. Fix a factorization $[1]\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{r}\mathbb J$ of the arrow-to-isomorphism functor with $i$ a cofibration and $r$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Such a factorization exists, and $K$ is cofibrant. For a small simplicial category $D$, a small set $V$, and a specified vertex arrow $v$ of $D$ for each label $v\in V$, define the ordinary pushout
$$\Gamma(D,V)=D\amalg_{\coprod_{v\in V}[1]}\coprod_{v\in V}K.$$
The canonical map $D\to\Gamma(D,V)$ represents $D\to L_VD$ under a natural isomorphism $\Gamma(D,V)\cong L_VD$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ under $D$. The construction is a strict functor on pairs: a simplicial functor $F:D\to D'$ and a label function $s:V\to V'$ with $F(v)=s(v)$ induce a map of pushouts, respecting identities and composition. If $s$ is the identity of a common label set and $F$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, the induced $\Gamma(D,V)\to\Gamma(D',V)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. If a simplicial functor $g:D\to T$ sends all labelled arrows to identity vertices, it has a specified extension $\bar g:\Gamma(D,V)\to T$: on the copy of $K$ for $v$, use $K\xrightarrow{r}\mathbb J\to\{g(\operatorname{source}v)\}\to T$. These extensions are natural for maps of pairs and for postcomposition by simplicial functors.

proof.text: In the Dwyer–Kan model structure of the inversion node, factor the arrow-to-isomorphism map [1]→𝕁 as a cofibration i:[1]→K followed by a Dwyer–Kan equivalence r:K→𝕁. The interval-lifting generators show that [1] is cofibrant: adjoin two isolated objects and then the generating arrow, so ∅→[1] is a cofibration. Hence ∅→K is a composite of cofibrations and K is cofibrant. Small coproducts of these cofibrations are cofibrations: a lifting square from a coproduct against a trivial fibration is solved summand by summand and the lifts are assembled by the coproduct universal property, and the empty coproduct is the identity of the initial object, which lifts against everything. Thus A=∐_V[1]→B=∐_VK is a cofibration, and all coproducts and pushouts used below exist in the fixed universe.

source.place: Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Proposition A.3.5.5, printed pp.891–893; the strict pushout and its homotopy-category mapping property.

proof.text: The strict-localization comparison recorded in [lem-coef-simplicial-strict-pushout-derived-comparison] applies to A=∐_V[1]→B=∐_VK and to the arbitrary map A→D: it identifies the actual ordinary pushout P=D amalgamated over A with B with the derived pushout of D←A→B in h sCat, under D. Thus the strict pushout used to define Γ(D,V) is a valid representative of the derived pushout, including repeated or coincident attaching vertices and V=∅. The derived-pushout mapping comparison of the cited node therefore applies to this actual P; no cofibrancy or left-properness hypothesis on D is used.

source.place: Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Proposition A.3.5.5, printed pp.891–893; the strict pushout and its homotopy-category mapping property.

proof.text: Put J_V=∐_V𝕁. The map r_V:B→J_V is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence, checked summand by summand: each mapping map is r, maps between distinct summands are empty on both sides, and essential surjectivity holds in every summand, with the empty coproduct included. The strict-pushout comparison node identifies the ordinary pushout P=D amalgamated over A with B with the derived pushout of D←A→B, naturally under D. (No such claim is made or needed for the ordinary pushout D amalgamated over A with J_V, which in general is not the derived pushout, since A→J_V is not a cofibration.) The map of spans (1_D,1_A,r_V) from D←A→B to D←A→J_V has weak-equivalence components, so by the derived-pushout mapping comparison the homotopy-pullback descriptions of Map^h(−,T) of the two derived pushouts are compared by a natural weak equivalence, using homotopy invariance of Map^h(−,T) in the B-variable; taking π₀ gives natural Hom bijections in h sCat compatible with restriction to D. The Yoneda argument on these bijections makes the induced map of derived pushouts an isomorphism under D. The derived pushout of D←A→J_V is L_VD by the definition in the inversion-universal-property node, so P≅L_VD naturally under D.

source.place: Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Proposition A.3.5.5, printed pp.891–893; the strict pushout and its homotopy-category mapping property.

proof.text: For a map of pairs (F,s):(D,V)→(D′,V′), map the v-copy of [1] and K to the s(v)-copy. The equality F(v)=s(v) makes the cocones compatible, so the pushout universal property supplies Γ(F,s). On identities and composites the two induced maps agree on both coprojections; uniqueness gives strict identity and composition laws. Repeated labels, noninjective s, and coincident endpoints are allowed.

source.place: Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Proposition A.3.5.5, printed pp.891–893; the strict pushout and its homotopy-category mapping property.

proof.text: Assume s is the identity of a common V and F is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence. Since h sCat is the localization at Dwyer–Kan equivalences, precomposition with F is a bijection on Hom sets in h sCat. Because F carries each labelled vertex v to the corresponding labelled vertex, this bijection restricts to a bijection between classes whose induced π₀-functors send every labelled arrow to an isomorphism. The inversion-universal-property node identifies those restricted subsets with Hom(L_VD′,T) and Hom(L_VD,T), naturally in T. Yoneda therefore makes L_VF an isomorphism in h sCat. The strict-pushout comparison node and Step 3's identifications P≅L_VD and P′≅L_VD′ identify Γ(F,1_V) with a representative of this isomorphism, so the image of Γ(F,1_V) in h sCat is an isomorphism; by [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences], applied to the Dwyer–Kan model structure and its localization h sCat, a map whose image in the homotopy category is an isomorphism is a weak equivalence, hence Γ(F,1_V) is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence.

source.place: Notation A.3.5.1, Remark A.3.5.2 and Proposition A.3.5.5, printed pp.891–893; the strict pushout and its homotopy-category mapping property.

proof.text: If g:D→T sends each labelled arrow to an identity vertex, its source and target agree at an object t_v. Collapse 𝕁 to its one-object terminal simplicial category at t_v and precompose with r:K→𝕁. On [1] this is exactly g on the labelled arrow, so these maps and g define the specified extension ḡ:P→T by the pushout universal property. For maps of pairs or postcomposition H:T→T′, the proposed extensions agree on D and on each K-copy; uniqueness gives the stated naturality equalities. The empty family returns g itself.
